manifest.source: COLBRYAN Technologies; aligned to the official JAMB IBASS subject syllabuses

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A runner covers 200 m in 25 s. What is the runner's average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time, giving 200/25 = 8 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A car travelling at 18 m/s brakes uniformly to rest in 6 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by time: (0-18)/6 = -3 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A stone is dropped from rest for 3 s where g = 10 m/s². How far does it fall?
questions.explanation: For motion from rest, distance is one-half gt squared, giving 45 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A passenger moves forward when a bus stops suddenly. Which property explains this motion?
questions.explanation: Inertia makes the passenger's body tend to continue its previous forward motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A 12 N horizontal force moves a box 5 m in its direction. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work equals force multiplied by displacement in the force direction, so 12 × 5 = 60 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A machine receives 500 J and delivers 350 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: Efficiency is useful output divided by input times 100, so 350/500 gives 70%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which circuit arrangement gives each household appliance the full supply voltage?
questions.explanation: Parallel branches place every appliance directly across the same supply voltage.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series. What is their total resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistances connected in series add directly, giving 4 + 6 = 10 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A 100 W lamp operates for 5 hours. How much electrical energy does it use?
questions.explanation: Energy in kilowatt-hours is 0.1 kW multiplied by 5 hours, which equals 0.5 kWh.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An echo returns 0.4 s after a shout. If sound travels at 340 m/s, how far away is the wall?
questions.explanation: The sound makes a return journey, so distance is 340 × 0.4 divided by 2 = 68 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Light passes from air into glass and bends toward the normal. What happens to its speed?
questions.explanation: Glass has a higher refractive index than air, so light travels more slowly in it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: An element has atomic number 13. How many protons are in each neutral atom?
questions.explanation: Atomic number is defined as the number of protons in an atom's nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Two atoms have the same proton number but different neutron numbers. How are they related?
questions.explanation: Isotopes share an atomic number but have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: An ion contains 17 protons and 18 electrons. Which symbol correctly represents its charge?
questions.explanation: One more electron than protons produces a single negative charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: In a chlorine molecule, what holds the two chlorine atoms together?
questions.explanation: Each chlorine atom contributes one electron to form a single covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Why does solid sodium chloride fail to conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: The charged ions are fixed in the solid lattice and cannot carry current through it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Diamond and graphite are both carbon, yet graphite conducts electricity. What enables this?
questions.explanation: Each graphite carbon leaves one electron delocalised and able to carry charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Blue litmus paper is placed in an acidic solution. What colour does it become?
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red under ordinary indicator conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Hydrochloric acid reacts completely with sodium hydroxide. Which salt is produced?
questions.explanation: The sodium ion combines with the chloride ion to form sodium chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A solution changes from pH 3 to pH 5. By what factor does its hydrogen-ion concentration decrease?
questions.explanation: Each pH unit represents a factor of ten, so two units represent a hundredfold decrease.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Which reagent can distinguish ethene from ethane at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Ethene rapidly decolourises bromine water by addition across its double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate under reflux. What organic product forms?
questions.explanation: Strong oxidation under reflux converts the primary alcohol fully to ethanoic acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Which organelle contains chlorophyll and traps light energy in a leaf cell?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll pigments within chloroplasts absorb light for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A plant cell becomes firm after immersion in pure water. What pressure develops inside it?
questions.explanation: Water entering by osmosis makes the contents press against the cell wall as turgor pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A secretory cell makes many protein enzymes. Which two organelles should be especially abundant?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes build proteins and rough endoplasmic reticulum processes and transports them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Which molecule carries inherited instructions in chromosomes?
questions.explanation: DNA stores genetic information in the sequence of its nucleotide bases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A homozygous red flower RR is crossed with a white flower rr, with red dominant. What colour are all F1 flowers?
questions.explanation: Every offspring receives R from one parent and r from the other, producing red Rr plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A mother is a carrier of an X-linked recessive trait and the father is unaffected. What fraction of their sons is expected to be affected?
questions.explanation: Each son receives his single X chromosome from the mother, with a one-half chance of the recessive allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: In a food chain, which organisms convert sunlight into stored chemical energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthetic producers capture light energy and store it in organic molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Lichens begin growing on bare rock after a volcanic eruption. What type of succession is starting?
questions.explanation: Primary succession begins where no developed soil or previous community remains.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legume root nodules benefit the plant by supplying what?
questions.explanation: The bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen into compounds the plant can use to build proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Which hormone lowers blood glucose after a carbohydrate-rich meal?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and storage, lowering its concentration in blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Why are alveoli efficient surfaces for gas exchange?
options: They provide a large, thin, well-supplied surface
They actively pump air into blood
questions.explanation: Numerous alveoli, thin moist walls and dense capillaries support rapid diffusion.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The price of tea stays constant while coffee becomes more expensive. What is likely to happen to demand for tea?
questions.explanation: Consumers may substitute tea for the now more expensive coffee, increasing tea demand.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A good has price elasticity of demand greater than one. How is its demand described?
questions.explanation: Demand is elastic when quantity responds proportionately more than price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A farmer's improved technology lowers production costs. What happens to the crop's supply curve?
questions.explanation: Lower costs make producers willing to supply more at each price, shifting supply right.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A town has only one legal electricity distributor. Which market structure best describes it?
questions.explanation: A monopoly exists where a single supplier serves the market.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Restaurants sell differentiated meals while many firms can enter. Which structure fits this market?
questions.explanation: Many sellers with differentiated products and relatively free entry characterise monopolistic competition.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Why can a price-discriminating firm charge different customers different prices?
options: It can separate markets and limit resale
questions.explanation: Market separation and restricted resale let the firm exploit different demand elasticities.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A trader accepts mobile money today for goods sold. Which function of money is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Money acts as a medium of exchange when it settles a purchase directly.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A commercial bank keeps part of deposits and lends the rest. What process can this support?
questions.explanation: Repeated lending and redepositing allows the banking system to expand deposit money.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The central bank sells government securities to commercial banks. What is the likely effect on liquidity?
options: It is unaffected in all cases
questions.explanation: Payment for the securities withdraws reserves from banks and reduces their lending capacity.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A country's output grows by 4% while its population grows by 6%. What likely happens to output per person?
questions.explanation: Population is growing faster than total output, so average output per person declines.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Why can investment in primary education promote long-term economic development?
options: It builds human capital and productivity
questions.explanation: Education raises skills, adaptability and productive capacity across the workforce.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A map arrow points to the top and is labelled N. Which direction lies to the right?
questions.explanation: With north at the top of a standard map, east lies to the right.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A river crosses contour lines whose V shapes point uphill. In which direction does the river flow?
options: Opposite the point of each V
Toward the point of each V
questions.explanation: Contour V shapes point upstream, so water flows in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A map uses a scale of 1:25,000. What ground distance is represented by 8 cm?
questions.explanation: Eight centimetres represents 200,000 cm, which converts to 2 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which weather element is measured with a wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer?
questions.explanation: The temperature difference between the bulbs is used to determine relative humidity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Why does equatorial rainfall commonly peak in the afternoon?
questions.explanation: Intense surface heating makes moist air rise, cool and condense into convectional storms.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A dry descending wind warms as it moves down a mountain's leeward side. Which condition results there?
questions.explanation: Descending air warms and dries, leaving the leeward side with reduced rainfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which census value is found by subtracting deaths from births, excluding migration?
questions.explanation: Natural increase is the excess of births over deaths in a population.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A population pyramid has a very broad base and narrow top. What does this usually indicate?
options: High birth rate and youthful population
Low birth rate and ageing population
questions.explanation: Many young people relative to older groups create a broad-based pyramid.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A city grows outward and absorbs nearby villages. Which urban process is occurring?
questions.explanation: Outward urban growth converts and incorporates surrounding rural settlements.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which resource is non-renewable on a human timescale?
questions.explanation: Crude oil forms over geological time and is depleted far faster than it is replaced.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: How does crop rotation with legumes help maintain soil fertility?
questions.explanation: Legume-associated bacteria add usable nitrogen compounds to the soil system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A government limits fishing during breeding seasons. Which resource-management principle is applied?
questions.explanation: Seasonal limits allow fish stocks to reproduce so future harvests can continue.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Citizens can find all major constitutional rules in one authoritative document. How is this constitution classified?
questions.explanation: A written constitution codifies its fundamental provisions in an authoritative text.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Which constitutional feature divides powers between central and regional governments?
questions.explanation: Federalism constitutionally allocates authority to two levels of government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A bill of rights protects speech but allows narrow public-safety limits. What must courts chiefly assess?
options: Whether the restriction is lawful and proportionate
questions.explanation: Courts assess whether a rights limitation has legal authority and is justified proportionately.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Which institution normally debates and passes national bills?
questions.explanation: The legislature considers proposed laws and enacts approved bills.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A president refuses assent to a bill and parliament may reconsider it. What does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Each branch has a power that checks the action of another branch.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Why is security of tenure important for judges?
options: It lets judges write party manifestos
It removes the need for evidence
It supports decisions free from political dismissal
questions.explanation: Protected tenure reduces pressure from officials who might dislike judicial decisions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A document lists a party's promised policies before an election. What is it called?
questions.explanation: A party manifesto presents its programme and promises to voters.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Why do parties hold primary elections?
questions.explanation: Primaries allow a party to select candidates for the general election.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Several small parties form an alliance to command a legislative majority. What have they created?
questions.explanation: A coalition combines parties so they can cooperate in forming or supporting government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A state officially accepts another new state as a member of the international community. What act is this?
questions.explanation: Recognition is formal acceptance of another state or government in international relations.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A country recalls its ambassador to protest another state's action. Which tool is being used?
questions.explanation: Recalling an ambassador signals official displeasure through diplomatic channels.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Two countries submit a territorial dispute to an international court. What peaceful method is this?
questions.explanation: Judicial settlement asks an agreed international tribunal to decide the legal dispute.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: The words 'buzz', 'hiss' and 'clang' imitate sounds. Which device do they exemplify?
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeic words imitate or suggest the sounds they describe.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: In 'the crown announced a new policy', what does 'the crown' represent?
questions.explanation: The associated object stands for the institution, making this an example of metonymy.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: A speaker says 'freedom is a cage' to express a troubling contradiction. Which device is central?
questions.explanation: The apparently self-contradictory statement invites a deeper interpretation, forming a paradox.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: What is the written conversation between characters in a play called?
questions.explanation: Dialogue is the spoken exchange written for characters in a dramatic work.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: A brief remark is spoken so the audience hears it but other characters supposedly do not. What is it?
questions.explanation: An aside gives the audience information while remaining unheard by other characters.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: A comic scene appears immediately after a tense death scene. What effect can this contrast create?
options: Proof that the death was historical
questions.explanation: Comic relief briefly eases tension and can sharpen the surrounding tragic mood.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: What term describes the recurring pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse?
questions.explanation: Meter organises rhythmic stresses into a recurring poetic pattern.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: A fourteen-line poem follows a recognised argument and rhyme pattern. What form is it likely to be?
questions.explanation: A sonnet is conventionally a fourteen-line poem with an organised structure.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: The speaker directly addresses the absent moon as if it could listen. Which device is used?
questions.explanation: Apostrophe addresses an absent person, abstract idea or non-human thing directly.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: Which element identifies when and where the events of a story occur?
questions.explanation: Setting establishes the story's place, time and surrounding social conditions.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: A novel interrupts present action to narrate the hero's childhood. Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: A flashback moves the narrative to events that happened before the present action.

questions.subject: Literature
questions.prompt: Readers know only what one third-person character observes and thinks. Which viewpoint is this?
questions.explanation: Third-person limited narration confines knowledge to the perspective of one focal character.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: A flowchart diamond normally represents which kind of operation?
questions.explanation: A diamond contains a condition whose outcomes send execution along different paths.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: A loop executes five times and adds 2 on each pass, starting from zero. What final value is produced?
questions.explanation: Five additions of two produce a total of 10.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: Which sorting method repeatedly compares neighbouring items and swaps them when out of order?
questions.explanation: Bubble sort uses repeated adjacent comparisons and swaps until the list is ordered.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: Which device connects computers within a local network and forwards frames by hardware address?
questions.explanation: An Ethernet switch learns hardware addresses and forwards frames within a LAN.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: What service converts a domain name such as example.com into an IP address?
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System resolves human-readable host names to network addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: Why does breaking a large message into packets improve network communication?
options: Packets can be routed and retransmitted independently
questions.explanation: Independent packets share routes efficiently and only missing pieces need retransmission.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: A laptop needs fast internal storage that uses flash memory and has no spinning parts. Which device fits?
questions.explanation: A solid-state drive stores data in electronic flash memory without moving components.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: Why is cache memory placed close to the processor?
options: To connect the computer to mains power
To provide frequently used data with very low delay
questions.explanation: Fast nearby cache reduces the time the processor waits for commonly needed instructions and data.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: A processor has four cores. What main advantage can this provide?
options: Several instruction streams can run in parallel
Every program becomes four times smaller
questions.explanation: Multiple cores can execute separate tasks or threads concurrently when software supports it.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: Which data type is most appropriate for storing whether a user is logged in?
questions.explanation: A Boolean stores one of two logical states, such as true or false.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: A function receives a value through a named variable in its definition. What is that variable called?
questions.explanation: A parameter is the named input through which a function receives an argument.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.prompt: A program catches a file-not-found error and shows a helpful message. Which practice is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Exception handling lets software respond safely to runtime errors instead of crashing abruptly.
